feedback: If the child says the 0 'means nothing', rebuild 30 with rods and no cubes and point to the empty ones spot: that empty spot IS the zero — zero ones. Contrast 3 and 30 to show the 0 keeps the 3 in the tens place (and, if ready, 300, where two zeros hold the 3 in the hundreds place) — zeros act as place-holders in their own place.
If the child reads the 3 at face value ('three'), count the ones inside the three rods (30) and say '3 in the tens place = 3 tens = 30'.
When the child adds the loose cube and 30 becomes 31, affirm: the 0 was doing real work holding the ones place empty; once a one is there, the ones digit reads 1.
Praise explanations that state both parts: '3 tens AND 0 ones'.
activities.intendedInsight: A decade is a whole number of tens with the ones column filled by zero; the 0 is a place-holder that keeps the tens digit in the tens place and marks that there are no ones. Decades are not a separate kind of number — they are the ones-is-zero case of tens-and-ones.
learnerActions: Set up a tens|ones chart (drawn or physical) with two columns.
Add tens rods one at a time into the tens column, placing no unit cubes; after each rod, say the count aloud: 'ten, twenty, thirty …' and write the numeral (10, 20, 30).
Each time, write a 0 in the ones column so the empty ones place is seen, not left blank.
Build 30 with three rods and say '30 is 3 tens and 0 ones'; build 50 with five rods and say '50 is 5 tens and 0 ones'.
Rebuild 30 with three rods, then add a single loose ones cube and read what you have: 30 becomes 31. Describe what the 0 was doing before you added the cube.
Optionally mark each decade on a 0-100 number line or bead string so the spoken word, the tens count, and the position all line up.
activities.title: Building decades with tens rods and a visible zero

feedback: For thirteen/thirty and fifteen/fifty mix-ups, build 13 (one ten and three ones) beside 30 (three tens, zero ones) so the structural difference is visible, and stress the ending sounds.
For a face-value or 'means nothing' answer about the 0, return to building the decade with rods and the empty ones column.
activities.intendedInsight: Children can recognise and justify decades across different representations, and can avoid confusing '-teen' words with '-ty' words.
learnerActions: Put the decade numerals in order smallest to largest (10, 20 … 90).
Match each decade numeral to a picture of the correct number of tens rods.
Fill in blanks such as '30 = __ tens' and '50 = 5 tens and __ ones'.
Choose and explain the meaning of the 0 in a decade (zero ones / place-holder), not 'nothing'.
Distinguish sound-alike pairs: thirteen vs thirty, fifteen vs fifty — say which is 'teen' (ten and some) and which is 'ty' (whole tens).
activities.title: Consolidation: sequence, match, and justify the zero

feedback: Accept answers that connect the 0 to 'zero ones' and to keeping the 3 in the tens place; gently redirect answers that treat the 0 as decorative.
If talk alone stalls, hand over rods so the argument can be grounded in a build.
activities.intendedInsight: Articulating the reason makes the place-holder role of the 0 explicit: it keeps the 3 in the tens place and marks zero ones.
learnerActions: Discuss the question: 'Why does 30 need a zero? What would happen if we just wrote 3?'
Use rods or a chart to argue your case: show that without the 0, the 3 would sit in the ones place and mean three.
Explain to a partner or adult why 30 is not the same as 3, and what the 0 is holding.
activities.title: 'Convince me the zero matters' discussion
